meta.title: Drawing Statistics — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Sample extension for Open 2D Studio that counts the shapes in a drawing by type. Adds an Add-Ins tab with a Shape Count button and the command stats show.

header.label: Extension for Open 2D Studio
header.title: Drawing Statistics
header.tagline: What is actually in your drawing?
header.desc: A small sample extension that counts the shapes in the current drawing by type. It adds an Add-Ins tab with a Shape Count button and the command stats show, and so shows how an extension for Open 2D Studio is put together.

cta.related: Read how extensions fit into the OpenAEC architecture

slides.standards: The Open 2D Studio Drawing Standards window with gridline dimensioning and the hatching per material

notice.text: Good to know: Open 2D Studio has been succeeded by Open CAD Studio. This extension is written for the Open 2D Studio extension API and mainly serves as an example.

features.label: Features
features.heading: A count of your drawing
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

ribbon.title: A tab of its own in the ribbon
ribbon.desc: The extension creates an Add-Ins tab, with a large Shape Count button in the Statistics group. One click shows the number of shapes in the drawing. Other extensions can use the same tab.

count.title: By type, with the total
count.desc: The count goes through every entity in the current drawing and lists them alphabetically by type, with the total at the top. If the drawing is empty, the extension says so.

command.title: From the command line too
command.desc: Type stats show in the Open 2D Studio terminal and you get the same count back as text. Handy in a series of commands or for copying.

example.title: A starting point for your own extension
example.desc: Two files and no build step: manifest.json describes the extension and the permissions it needs, main.js calls the Open 2D Studio API in onLoad. Copy the repository and build on it.

ribbon.title: Add-Ins tab
ribbon.desc: A tab of its own in the ribbon, with the Shape Count button in the Statistics group.

terminal.title: Terminal command
terminal.desc: The command stats show returns the count as text.

count.title: Count by type
count.desc: Every entity in the current drawing, alphabetically by type and with the total.

readonly.title: Read only
readonly.desc: The extension reads the list of entities and changes nothing in your drawing.

manifest.desc: Name, version, minimum app version, category, tags and the permissions of the extension.

main.title: main.js
main.desc: Plain JavaScript without a build step, with an onLoad and an onUnload function.

api.desc: Adding a tab and a button, registering a command and requesting the entities of the drawing.

what.a: A small sample extension for Open 2D Studio. It counts the shapes in the current drawing by type and shows how an extension adds a tab, a button and a command to the application.

install.q: How do I install the extension?
install.a: Download the zip file. In the desktop version of Open 2D Studio, open the app menu, choose Extensions and then Install from file…, and select the zip. The extension is unpacked into the Open 2D Studio extensions folder and loaded right away.

version.q: Which version of Open 2D Studio do I need?

count.q: What exactly does the extension count?
count.a: Every entity in the current drawing, by type, with the total at the top. If the drawing is empty, the extension reports that there are no shapes.

permissions.q: Which permissions does the extension ask for?
permissions.a: Three: commands for the command stats show, ribbon for the tab and the button, and events. The extension only reads the list of entities in the drawing and changes nothing.

build.q: Can I make an extension myself?
build.a: Yes. This extension consists of two files: manifest.json with name, version, minimum app version and permissions, and main.js with an onLoad function that uses the Open 2D Studio API. Use the repository as a starting point.
